paragraphs: A spot cleaner is a wet vacuum small enough to be carried to the accident. Two tanks, one clean and one dirty, a brush head and a hose, all built around the fact that the stain is usually somewhere a full machine cannot reach.
The model is dense for its size at 554,592 polygons and 285,845 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits close product work. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits appliance and product visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, interior and cleaning scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

Agricultural implement tyres are a different problem from tractor tyres. They carry weight without driving, run on roads and in fields, and the rib pattern exists to steer and resist sinking rather than to grip.
The model is light at 23,525 polygons and 23,307 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 5 maps all at 4096x4096. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits agricultural and vehicle parts visualisation, tyre marketing, e-commerce imagery, technical illustration, game assets and editorial work. On sale since 2026.

Desk organisers are sold on the promise that tidiness is a purchasable state. The drawer is the interesting part: everything visible has to look deliberate, so the compartment that hides the mess is what makes the object work.
The model is light at 50,544 polygons and 25,832 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied with the pencil. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits product and stationery visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, office and interior scenes, advertising, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

An engorged tick is a completely different shape from a hungry one, which is why they are so often misidentified. The body expands many times over while the legs and mouthparts stay exactly the same size, and the proportions become genuinely alarming.
The model is very light at 7,445 polygons and 7,549 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, groomed with fur and rigged so it can be posed. It is built to CheckMate specification.

At $39 it suits medical and veterinary education, public health material, pest control and outdoor safety visualisation, documentary graphics, game assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Wrought iron garden furniture is uncomfortable, heavy and impossible to steal, and it has outlasted every lighter alternative for exactly those reasons. It is bought once and stays outside for decades, acquiring the patina that is half the appeal.
The model holds 48,438 polygons and 49,614 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in blue. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits garden and exterior visualisation, architectural and landscape scenes, furniture marketing, e-commerce imagery, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2023.

A weapons trolley is a hydraulic table on castors, and the whole design is about the last few centimetres: lifting a heavy store to exactly the right height under a wing so it can be pushed onto the pylon by hand.
The model is light at 24,383 polygons and 25,316 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.
At $39 it suits aviation and defence visualisation, ground support equipment presentation, flight line scenes, training material, film props and game environments. On sale since 2024.

Ten gauge is the large end of what anybody actually shoulders, and the shells look it. The box is designed to be recognised on a shelf at a glance, because the one thing that must never happen is picking up the wrong gauge by mistake.
The model is very light at 8,858 polygons and 8,811 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 10 maps all at 2048x2048. It carries StemCell certification.
At $39 it suits product and packaging visualisation, retail and e-commerce imagery, film and television props, game assets, hunting scenes and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

Premium packaging borrows its language from tobacco and spirits because that is where the visual grammar of an adult product already exists. An open box, contents visible and arranged, is the oldest presentation trick in the category.
The model holds 286,000 polygons and 320,877 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied open. It carries StemCell certification.
At $39 it suits packaging and product visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, dispensary and interior scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Soft luggage survives because it gives. A hard case protects contents and then cannot be forced into an overhead locker; a soft one compresses, absorbs an extra jumper and still fits, which is the trade most travellers actually make.
The model is light at 32,109 polygons and 32,984 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in brown, and carries StemCell certification.
At $39 it suits luggage and retail visualisation, e-commerce and catalogue imagery, travel advertising, character accessories, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

Aerofoil crossbars exist because the old square ones made a noise at motorway speed that drove owners to remove the rack entirely. Solving the whistle was worth more commercially than any improvement in load capacity.
The model is built at subdivision level, 84,124 polygons and 85,288 vertices with non-overlapping UVs, so it holds up close. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits automotive accessory visualisation, aftermarket and e-commerce imagery, vehicle configurators, outdoor and travel scenes, game assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

The flip key was a brief and clever answer to a real problem: a blade long enough to turn a lock is too long to sit in a pocket. Folding it solved that, and then keyless entry made the whole question irrelevant within a decade.

The model is extremely light at 5,339 polygons and 5,464 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, folded, textured with 4 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits automotive product visualisation, accessory and e-commerce imagery, advertising, close up and interior scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2018.

A radiator is a heat exchanger that has to survive stones. The core is as thin as it can be made without being destroyed by road debris, and the fan behind it exists only for the times the car is not moving fast enough to cool itself.

The model is light at 28,203 polygons and 31,598 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 8 maps, 6 at 4096x4096 and 2 at 512x512, supplied with the fan. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a motor radiator build is offered separately.
At $39 it suits automotive parts visualisation, technical and training material, aftermarket and e-commerce imagery, engine bay scenes, game assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2018.

Spirits bottles are shaped to be recognised through a shelf of competitors, which is why the silhouette matters more than the label. A wide shoulder and a short neck read as premium for reasons nobody in the industry can entirely explain.
The model is extremely light at 3,094 polygons and 3,104 vertices, built in quads only with mixed UV layout. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits beverage and packaging visualisation, label mockups, e-commerce and retail imagery, bar and hospitality scenes, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

A stack of cement bags is the unit that construction is actually measured in. The paper sack has barely changed in a century, the weight is set by what one person can lift badly, and a pallet of them is the first thing to arrive on any site.
The model holds 37,400 polygons and 39,600 vertices, built in quads only with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 6 maps all at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits construction and site visualisation, builders merchant and retail scenes, logistics presentation, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.
